iris-glow.$description: Iris Glow — Primary brand accent — headline words, diagram group borders, and the violet offset shadow that makes hero cards pop off the canvas

pale-lavender.$description: Pale Lavender — Softened brand accent — used where Iris Glow would be too saturated, particularly in headline strokes and lighter decorative borders

violet-deep.$description: Violet Deep — Accent shadow tone — paired with the 6px solid-offset shadow recipe to make Iris Glow feel grounded on the dark canvas

sky-pulse.$description: Sky Pulse — Cool accent — second headline color and decorative border accent; the blue counterpart to the violet brand system

saffron-whisper.$description: Saffron Whisper — Warm accent — third headline color, brings the gold/amber note into the multi-word display treatment

rose-quartz.$description: Rose Quartz — Warm accent — fourth headline color, the pink note that completes the four-color headline palette

bone.$description: Bone — Primary text and dominant border color across the interface — the single most-used color in the system

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Page canvas and card fill background — the dark base everything sits on

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Muted borders and dividers, secondary structural lines on dark surfaces

ink-black.$description: Ink Black — Deepest shadow tone — used in the 6px 6px 0 hard-offset shadow under standard cards

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Primary action fill — the only CTA button background; also used for high-emphasis text on dark surfaces

pearl.$description: Pearl — Secondary text color and heading borders where Bone is too cool

slate.$description: Slate — Subtle borders — the barely-there divider for low-emphasis separation

graphite.$description: Graphite — Muted text and link borders — body copy de-emphasized, nav text in resting state

ash.$description: Ash — Subtle link borders for de-emphasized text links

national-2-condensed.$description: Display and hero headlines only — used for the brand's biggest typographic statement. The 0.85 line-height is unusually tight and makes multi-line headlines stack like a poster, not flow like prose. Combined with -0.007em tracking and condensed proportions, this face carries authority without weight.

inter.$description: All UI text — body, nav, buttons, labels, subheadings, and card titles. The 400 weight is the workhorse; 600 is reserved for emphasis. The slight -0.019em tracking tightens UI text on the dark canvas, giving it the same technical-drawing precision as the display face. No 300 weight — restraint here means condensed, not thin.

jetbrains-mono.$description: Code and technical tokens — used for diagram node labels, code snippets, and any monospaced context. The 1.00 line-height variant is for inline monospaced glyphs.
